checks.detail: AC-7 is not_met (A Linear project that fails from the server's first read gets the wrong last good read. I ran a second server with the Linear proxy giving a GraphQL error for 'SDLC board' from the start. On the first read the app showed 'linear is stale (last good read 17:41 UTC, 7 s ago): 1 of 2 repos failed ... (no earlier tickets)'. On the next read, booking still read fine and the project still failed. The app then showed 'Last refreshed: ... linear 498761 h ago' and 'linear is stale (last good read 00:00 UTC, 498761 h ago): ... (kept its tickets from an earlier read)' (06-nevergood.png). It has no earlier tickets. A probe test in the scratch worktree did the same: last_good went Some(now), then Some(0), Some(0) (probe-never-good.log). The cause is in crates/server/src/linear.rs read(): a failed read with no earlier entry stores `last.unwrap_or_default()`, i.e. (0, []), so the next failure finds an entry. Otherwise AC-7 holds live. One project failing: from 17:36:42 the proxy failed 'SDLC board' only, and three reads failed (17:37:30, 17:38:30, 17:39:31). The app kept TRU-8 and TRU-11 (Blocked, though Linear's value was then Rollout). Booking kept updating: TRU-6 moved to PR review at 17:37:33. Linear's shown last good read stayed at '17:36 UTC' throughout and the age grew to 3 min (04-proj-18c.png, proj.log). After I removed the failure, the 17:40:32 read showed TRU-11 at Rollout and the error cleared. GitHub failing: injected 500s from 17:41. The 18:00:13 read failed, PRs #49 and #53 stayed, and the app showed 'github is stale (last good read 17:33 UTC, 27 min ago): ... 500 ...' while Linear kept updating (09-ghdown-6.png). With the server stopped, the app kept its board and showed 'Couldn't refresh ... Connection refused (os error 111)' (13-down-hold-back.png). The cluster part couldn't be exercised: the server has no cluster source yet.)

checks.name: no_blocking_findings
checks.detail: 1 open: crates/server/src/linear.rs read(): when a repo's read fails and it has no earlier tickets, `last.unwrap_or_default()` stores (0, []) as that repo's last read. On the next failure, `last.is_some()` is true, so the error says '(kept its tickets from an earlier read)' and as_of becomes Some(0). Linear's last_good is then 0. Observed live: a project failing from server start showed 'linear 498761 h ago' and 'last good read 00:00 UTC' on its second read, while the other repo read fine (06-nevergood.png). A probe test gave last_good Some(now), then Some(0), Some(0) (probe-never-good.log). AC-7's 'time of its last good read' is wrong here, and so is AC-6's 'when its data was last refreshed'.

crates/server/tests/sources.rs:one_failing_linear_project_keeps_its_tickets_and_the_other_repo_updates makes only one failing read. A mutant that restamps the kept tickets with now() on each failure (`last.map(|(_, i)| (now(), i))`) still passes, though it moves last_good forward from the second failure on. The real code held 17:36:29 across three live failures.

crates/app/tests/board.rs:ages_go_by_the_servers_clock finishes only one read. A mutant that keeps the first read's `got` (`self.got.or(Some(Instant::now()))`) passes, though later snapshots would then show ages too large. Likewise, nothing checks that a same-repo sub-ticket doesn't name its repo: `if true` passes sub_tickets_are_drawn_under_their_ticket_with_their_stages.

Carried from round 2, still observed: a GitHub source with no good read yet says 'github is stale (no good read yet): ... (kept its PRs from an earlier read)' (06-nevergood.png). Still no test covers the ureq request deadline or the stale line's wrapping. Both were observed working live.

AC-7 names the cluster, but the server has no cluster source yet, so that part is unexercised. AC-6's 'PR checks finish within 2 minutes' holds only with GITHUB_TOKEN: tokenless, GitHub reads were 27 min apart (17:33:28, then 18:00:13), as docs/STATUS.md says. The device-clock check used an LD_PRELOAD CLOCK_REALTIME shim (verify3-tru11/scripts/fakeclock.c) because libfaketime isn't installed.
